app.name: Hejmo
firststeps.title: First steps
firststeps.lead: This is how you fill Hejmo with your family life. The order helps; every step can be skipped.
firststeps.skipped.text: Skipped. You can catch up any time.
firststeps.hide.hint: You will find them under Settings.
firststeps.settled: All done. Hejmo now knows your family.
firststeps.close.hint: After that the start page shows your day. You will find the steps under Settings.
firststeps.family.title: Add the family
firststeps.family.text: Add your partner and the children, up to 8 people. Each person gets a colour and a marker. This way even children who cannot read yet find themselves on the display.
firststeps.parents.title: Invite the second parent
firststeps.parents.text: Add the second parent. Then you connect your phones, so you always have Hejmo with you.
firststeps.calendars.title: Connect a calendar
firststeps.calendars.text: Connect iCloud, Google or another calendar. For each calendar you choose who it is for: the whole family or single people. Without a calendar of your own you use the box's calendar.
firststeps.tasks.title: Tasks or routine
firststeps.tasks.text: Add tasks that repeat, for example in the morning: brush teeth, get dressed, pack the school bag. Children earn stars for ticking them off.
firststeps.meals.title: Shopping list and meal plan
firststeps.meals.text: Plan the week's meals, and they show on the display. Put what you need on the shopping list.
firststeps.display.title: Hang the first display
firststeps.display.text: A tablet or E-Ink display on the wall shows your day, easy to see for everyone. Hejmo only asks you: "Where does it hang?"
flash.first_steps_hidden: First steps hidden. You will find them under Settings.
flash.first_steps_shown: First steps are back on the start page.
hub.first_steps.hint: Shows the steps that help you set up on the start page again.
setup.welcome.title: Welcome to Hejmo
setup.welcome.lead: You set up your box here. It takes about 15 minutes. You can stop in between: the box remembers how far you got.
setup.welcome.step.1: The box gets a certificate, so passwords and appointments are sent encrypted.
setup.welcome.step.2: Your town, your name, your password and a PIN for the display.
setup.welcome.step.3: An app on your phone shows you a code when you sign in. This protects your account.
setup.welcome.step.4: After that the start page guides you: add the family, connect a calendar, hang the first display. Every step can be skipped.
setup.welcome.need.app: Your phone with an authenticator app, for example [2FAS](https://2fas.com/), [Aegis](https://getaegis.app/) (Android only) or [Google Authenticator](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447).
setup.welcome.need.desec: For the recommended way: a free account at [deSEC](https://desec.io/signup). Step 1 shows you how.
setup.https.choice.title: How should people reach the box securely?
setup.https.choice.lead: Phones, tablets and computers talk to the box only in encrypted form. For that it needs a certificate. There are two ways.
setup.https.way.public.hint: The box gets a name like familie.dedyn.io. Every device trusts it at once, without installing anything. You need a free deSEC account. The name only points to your box at home; it cannot be reached from outside.
setup.https.way.own.hint: No account needed, nothing leaves your home. In return you install a certificate once on every phone, tablet and computer you open the box with.
setup.https.invalidhost: This address cannot be used for HTTPS. Open the box by its IP address or a name such as hejmo.local.
setup.https.own.title: Create the box's certificate
setup.https.own.lead: The box creates its own certificate. It is valid only for the box and cannot vouch for any other website.
setup.https.own.for: The certificate is valid for this address:
setup.https.own.hint: Always open the box under this address from now on. Under another name, the browser warns.
setup.https.public.title: Set up a public name
setup.https.public.lead: You get a name and an access token from deSEC. The box then gets the certificate itself.
setup.https.public.s1.title: Create an account at deSEC
setup.https.public.s1.text: deSEC is a non-profit association from Berlin. The account is free.
setup.https.public.s2.title: Create a name
setup.https.public.s2.text: At deSEC, open [Domains](https://desec.io/domains), create a name that ends in **.dedyn.io** and enter it here.
setup.https.public.s3.title: Create an access token
setup.https.public.s3.text: At deSEC, open [Token Management](https://desec.io/tokens), create a new token and paste it here. The box stores it encrypted.
setup.https.public.name: Name of the box
setup.https.public.lan_ip: Address of the box at home
setup.https.public.lan_ip.hint: Your devices reach the box in your home network under this address. Already filled in with the address you are using now.
setup.https.public.issuer.actalis.hint: From Italy (EU). Needs a free account; the box then asks for the key ID and HMAC key.
setup.https.public.email.hint: With an email address the box can fall back to ZeroSSL when Let's Encrypt cannot be reached.
setup.https.public.terms: With "Get certificate" you accept the terms of the chosen certificate authority.
setup.https.public.busy: The box is getting the certificate …
setup.https.public.busy.hint: This usually takes under a minute, at most 3 minutes. Keep this page open.
setup.https.public.failed: The box could not get the certificate. Most often the token is wrong, or the name does not belong to this deSEC account. Check both and try again.
setup.https.error.invalid: Please check your entries and try again.
setup.https.error.name: This name does not work. It needs at least one dot and only lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, for example familie.dedyn.io.
setup.https.error.lan_ip: That is not an address in your home network. It looks like this, for example: 192.168.178.40.
setup.https.error.eab: Enter the key ID and HMAC key of your Actalis account.
setup.https.error.token: Paste the access token from deSEC.
setup.https.error.token_again: Please paste the token again. The box does not keep it after an error.
setup.https.check.title: Check the name
setup.https.check.lead: The certificate is here. Now your browser checks whether it reaches the box under its new name.
setup.https.check.fail: Your browser does not reach **{name}** yet.
setup.https.check.last: This page checks again every 5 seconds. Last try: {time}
setup.https.check.ok: Your browser reaches the box under **{name}**.
setup.https.check.ok.hint: From now on, open the box under this name. It works on every device in your home network.
setup.https.rebind.title: Most often the router blocks the name
setup.https.rebind.why: The name points to an address in your home. Many routers refuse that as protection (DNS rebind protection). Add the name as an exception. On a FRITZ!Box it works like this:
setup.https.rebind.s1.title: Open the home network settings
setup.https.rebind.s1.text: Open [fritz.box](http://fritz.box/) and there [[Home Network › Network › Network settings › Additional settings › Home network]].
setup.https.rebind.s2.title: Add the exception
setup.https.rebind.s2.text: Under [[DNS rebind protection]] add this name:
setup.https.rebind.s3.title: Apply and check
setup.https.rebind.s3.text: Click "Apply" in the FRITZ!Box. This page notices by itself.
setup.https.rebind.other: Another router? Look in its settings for "DNS rebind protection" or a list of allowed names.
setup.https.ownca.title: Cannot change the router?
setup.https.ownca.text: Then use the box's own certificate. The public name is forgotten. Afterwards you install the certificate once on every device.
setup.title: Your account
setup.lead: This is how you sign in to Hejmo. You add other parents and the children afterwards.
setup.step.home.hint: The town gives the weather and the sunrise and sunset, the state the public holidays.
setup.step.pin.hint: Parents need the PIN at the display, for example to delete a whole list. Children should not know it.
setup.field.name: Your name
setup.field.name.hint: This is how you appear on the display.
setup.field.username.hint: You sign in with it. Lower-case letters are easiest.
setup.error.region: Please choose a state or canton.
setup.error.name: Please enter your name and a username.
setup.error.password: The password is too short. It needs at least 10 characters.
setup.error.code: That code is wrong. Use the code that is in the app right now. If it is wrong again, check that your phone's clock is right.
setup.totp.title: Set up the one-time code
setup.totp.lead: When you sign in you need, besides your password, a code from an app on your phone. This way nobody gets into your box with just your password.
setup.totp.s1.title: Open an authenticator app
setup.totp.s1.text: Open the app you use to create codes.
setup.totp.s1.install.desktop: Don't have one? 2FAS is free: [for iPhone in the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/2fas-auth/id1217793794) or [for Android on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.twofasapp). [Aegis](https://getaegis.app/) or [Google Authenticator](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447) work too.
setup.totp.s1.install.android: Don't have one? [Get 2FAS on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.twofasapp); it is free. [Aegis](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.beemdevelopment.aegis) works too.
setup.totp.s1.install.ios: Don't have one? [Get 2FAS in the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/2fas-auth/id1217793794); it is free. [Google Authenticator](https://apps.apple.com/app/google-authenticator/id388497605) works too.
setup.totp.scan.title: Scan the QR code
setup.totp.scan.text: In the app, tap "Add" or "+" and scan this code.
setup.totp.key: QR code does not work? Type the key
setup.totp.key.text: In the app, choose "Enter key" and type:
setup.totp.phone.title: Add Hejmo in the app
setup.totp.phone.text: Tap the button and choose your authenticator app.
setup.totp.other: The app is on another phone?
setup.totp.other.text: Scan this QR code with the other phone.
setup.totp.qr: QR code of the one-time code key. Scan it with the authenticator app.
setup.totp.s3.title: Enter the code
setup.totp.s3.text: The app now shows a 6-digit code for Hejmo. It changes every 30 seconds.
trust.title: Trust the box
trust.lead: For your device to trust the box, you install its certificate once. It is valid only for the box. This takes about 2 minutes.
trust.devices.label: Choose a device
trust.detected.unknown: Your device was not detected. Choose it.
trust.steps.title: {device}: 4 steps
trust.waiting: Your {device} does not trust the box yet.
trust.fail: Your {device} does not trust the box yet.
trust.fp.title: Compare the fingerprint (optional)
trust.fp.what: The fingerprint is like a serial number: every certificate has its own. If your device shows a **SHA-256** fingerprint while installing, it must look exactly like this. Compare at least the first and the last line.
trust.fp.mismatch: If it does not match, do not install the certificate. The box's log names the same fingerprint; comparing there is the stronger check.
trust.windows.mismatch: Windows shows only SHA-1, so there is nothing to compare while installing. Check the SHA-256 fingerprint above against the box log.
trust.skip.title: The check does not work?
trust.skip.text: Some browsers do not allow the check. If you did all the steps, you can continue anyway. If the browser then shows a warning, the certificate is still missing.
trust.later: You set up the family's other phones, tablets and computers later. When you connect a phone or display, the box shows you the way.
trust.ios.1.title: Download the profile
trust.ios.1.text: Tap the button. If your device asks whether it may download the profile, tap "Allow".
trust.ios.1.after: Downloaded. Next you install the profile.
trust.ios.2.title: Install the profile
trust.ios.2.text: Open [[Settings]]. At the top it says [[Profile Downloaded]]. Tap it, then "Install", and enter your device's passcode.
trust.ios.3.title: Turn on trust
trust.ios.3.text: Open [[Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings]] and turn on [[Hejmo box CA]].
trust.ios.3.fail: Is [[Hejmo box CA]] turned on in the certificate trust settings? It is a separate switch that only exists after installing.
trust.ios.4.title: Come back here
trust.ios.4.text: This page notices by itself when your device trusts the box.
trust.ios.fp: Where to find it: while installing, under "More Details".
trust.android.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.android.1.text: Tap the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.android.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.android.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.android.2.text: Open [[Settings › Security › More security settings › Install a certificate › CA certificate]] and choose hejmo-ca.crt.
trust.android.2.hint: The names differ a little by manufacturer. Search the settings for "CA certificate".
trust.android.3.title: Confirm the warning
trust.android.3.text: Android warns that someone could read along. The certificate is valid only for the box; tap "Install anyway".
trust.android.3.fail: Is the certificate installed as a "CA certificate"? As a "VPN and app user certificate" or "Wi-Fi certificate" it is not enough.
trust.android.4.title: Come back here
trust.android.4.text: Come back to this browser. This page notices by itself when your device trusts the box.
trust.android.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]], or it will not trust the box. Calendar apps such as DAVx5 ask once more when you first connect whether they should trust the certificate. Confirm it once.
trust.android.fp: Where to find it: Settings › Security › Trusted credentials › User › Hejmo box CA.
trust.mac.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.mac.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.mac.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.mac.2.title: Put it in the keychain
trust.mac.2.text: Open [[Keychain Access]], choose the keychain [[login]] on the left and drag hejmo-ca.crt into it. Do not double-click the file.
trust.mac.3.title: Always trust
trust.mac.3.text: Double-click [[Hejmo box CA]], expand [[Trust]] and under "When using this certificate" choose [[Always Trust]]. Close the window and confirm with your Mac password.
trust.mac.3.fail: Does [[Hejmo box CA]] say [[Always Trust]] under "Trust"? After closing the window the Mac asks for your password.
trust.mac.4.title: Come back here
trust.mac.4.text: This page notices by itself when your Mac trusts the box.
trust.mac.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.mac.fp: Where to find it: in Keychain Access at "Hejmo box CA" under "Fingerprints", SHA-256.
trust.windows.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.windows.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.windows.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.windows.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.windows.2.text: Double-click hejmo-ca.crt and choose [[Install Certificate]] and [[Current User]]. Then choose [[Place all certificates in the following store]], [[Browse]] and [[Trusted Root Certification Authorities]].
trust.windows.3.title: Confirm the warning
trust.windows.3.text: Windows warns about a new root certification authority. The certificate is valid only for the box; confirm with "Yes".
trust.windows.3.fail: Is the certificate in "Trusted Root Certification Authorities"? Firefox uses its own certificates, see below.
trust.windows.4.title: Come back here
trust.windows.4.text: This page notices by itself when your computer trusts the box.
trust.windows.after: Firefox uses its own certificates: [[Settings › Privacy & Security › View Certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.windows.fp: While installing, Windows shows only a SHA-1 fingerprint. It is not the same as the box's SHA-256 fingerprint, so compare the one above with the box log.
trust.linux.1.title: Download the certificate
trust.linux.1.text: Click the button. The file hejmo-ca.crt lands in your Downloads folder.
trust.linux.1.after: Downloaded: hejmo-ca.crt in your Downloads folder.
trust.linux.2.title: Install the certificate
trust.linux.2.text: Open a terminal in the Downloads folder. On Debian and Ubuntu enter: [[sudo cp hejmo-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && sudo update-ca-certificates]]
trust.linux.2.hint: Other distributions have their own folder for certificate authorities. Search for "add CA certificate" and your system's name.
trust.linux.3.title: Set up the browser
trust.linux.3.text: Chrome, Edge and Firefox use their own certificates. Import hejmo-ca.crt there under [[Settings › Privacy and security › Manage certificates › Authorities › Import]].
trust.linux.3.fail: Did you import hejmo-ca.crt in the browser as a certificate authority, with the tick for websites? The system alone is not enough for Chrome and Firefox.
trust.linux.4.title: Come back here
trust.linux.4.text: This page notices by itself when your computer trusts the box.
trust.linux.fp: Where to find it: in a terminal with [[openssl x509 -in hejmo-ca.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256]].

connections.title: iCloud and other calendar servers
connect.title: Connect a calendar
connect.lead: Hejmo fetches your events from where you already keep them. Nothing is changed or deleted at iCloud or on the server.
connect.icloud.name: iCloud
connect.icloud.sub: Calendars from iPhone, iPad and Mac
connect.caldav.name: Another calendar server
connect.caldav.sub: CalDAV, for example Nextcloud, Synology, mailbox.org or Posteo
connect.why.title: Why a separate password?
connect.icloud.link.label: account.apple.com
connect.done: Then you choose which calendars the box shows.
connect.icloud.heading: Connect iCloud
connect.icloud.why: Hejmo never asks for your Apple password. You create an app-specific password just for Hejmo at Apple, and you can revoke it there at any time without changing your Apple password.
connect.icloud.step1.title: Sign in at Apple
connect.icloud.step1.text: Open your Apple Account page and sign in.
connect.icloud.step1.hint: Opens in a new tab. Keep this page open and come back here afterwards.
connect.icloud.step2.title: Open App-Specific Passwords
connect.icloud.notfound.text: The item only appears when two-factor authentication is on for your Apple Account. Turn it on on your iPhone: [[Settings]], then your name, then [[Sign-In and Security]]. Then reload the Apple page.
connect.icloud.help.label: support.apple.com/en-us/102654
connect.icloud.step3.title: Create a password for Hejmo
connect.icloud.step3.text: Create a new password and name it [[Hejmo]]. Apple asks for your Apple password once more: you enter it at Apple, not here. Then copy the password Apple shows you.
connect.icloud.step4.title: Enter it here
connect.icloud.step4.text: Your normal Apple password never goes into Hejmo.
connect.icloud.username: Email address of your Apple Account
connect.icloud.password.hint: Four groups of four letters, separated by hyphens.
connect.caldav.heading: Connect another calendar server
connect.caldav.why: Many servers, Nextcloud included, offer app passwords. Your normal password stays with you, and you can withdraw Hejmo's access at any time.
connect.caldav.step1.title: Find the address of your calendar
connect.caldav.step1.text: On Nextcloud: open the [[Calendar]] app, then [[Calendar settings]] at the bottom left, then [[Copy primary CalDAV address]]. For other providers, the CalDAV address is in their help.
connect.caldav.help.label: Nextcloud help for the calendar
connect.caldav.step2.title: Create an app password
connect.caldav.step2.text: On Nextcloud: [[Personal settings]], then [[Security]], then [[Create new app password]]. Name it [[Hejmo]] and copy it. If your server offers no app passwords, use your normal password.
connect.caldav.step3.title: Enter it here
connect.caldav.url.hint: Starts with https://. On Nextcloud it usually ends in /remote.php/dav.
connect.caldav.single: The address is a single calendar, not the whole server
connections.empty: No connection yet. Connect iCloud or another calendar server, and your events appear on the box.

connections.error.server_saved: The server cannot be reached or offers no calendars. Try again later.

connections.choose.none: No calendars were found on this server.

connections.error.calendar: That address is not on the server of this connection.
connections.error.login: The server refused the user name or password. For iCloud, create a new app-specific password at Apple and connect the calendar again.
connections.error.foreign_host: The server pointed to a different domain. For your safety the password is only sent to the server you entered.

https.warning: The box's HTTPS certificate could not be renewed or loaded. Devices will refuse to connect once it has expired or is missing.
https.warning.hint: Check the DNS token and that the box is online; it tries again automatically. If the certificate authority or deSEC cannot be reached, waiting helps; if the key file secret.key was lost, restore it from your backup. Until then the box may serve its own certificate: install the box certificate on the phones (page /ca) so they trust it.
caldav.title: Calendar apps
caldav.intro: Phones and calendar apps (iOS Calendar, DAVx5 and others) can subscribe to the box's calendars and save events back. Add a calendar account of type CalDAV with the address and user name below. As the password, use a device token created here: one per device, revoked on its own.

caldav.token.name: Device name, for example "iPhone Mama"
caldav.calendars.intro: The family calendar is always available. Subscribed calendars are shared through the box if you switch it on; calendars from other services are better added on the phone directly.
caldav.profile.title: Set up an iPhone or iPad in one step
caldav.profile.intro: Download an iPhone profile that sets up the calendar account for you: server address, your user name and a new device token are inside. Open the file directly on the iPhone or iPad, install it under "Profile Downloaded" in Settings, and delete the file afterwards.
caldav.profile.ca_first: Your box uses its own certificate: install the box's certificate profile on the device first.
caldav.profile.once: The box keeps no copy. The file holds the token in plain text; to get one again, create a new profile, which creates a new token. Removing the profile on the device does not revoke the token: do that under Device tokens.
caldav.profile.error.https: The profile holds a password and is only offered over HTTPS. Open the box through its HTTPS address.

mcp.explain.title: What is MCP?
mcp.explain.what: AI assistants such as Claude or ChatGPT can do more than answer questions: they can also look things up in other programs and enter things. **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is the common language for this. When you switch MCP on, your Hejmo box understands that language.
mcp.explain.say: You can then say to the assistant, for example:
mcp.explain.say1: “Add Mia's parents' evening on Tuesday at 7:30 pm.”
mcp.explain.say2: “Put milk and oats on the shopping list.”
mcp.explain.say3: “Plan five quick dinners for next week.”
mcp.explain.may1: Only what you choose for the token: events, lists, tasks (with routines and stars) and the meal plan, each read only or also changing.
mcp.explain.may2: Never: change settings, create tokens, manage people, displays or phones.
mcp.explain.know1: What the assistant reads, it sends to its provider so the AI can answer. Give it only the areas it needs.
mcp.explain.know2: A token belongs to the parent who creates it; the assistant acts as that person. Children get no MCP token.
mcp.explain.know3: The box speaks MCP only encrypted (HTTPS). It is usually reachable only on your home network; then the assistant has to run on a device on your home network. The guide shows how.
